title: incident-bot: concise runbook linking + auto-diagnostics context enrichment
author: Priya Natarajan
description: Motivation: On-call responders frequently need a short, actionable runbook link and a minimal SLO/diagnostic summary when an incident is triaged. The incident-bot currently posts full runbook links and long context dumps which increase cognitive load and slack noise. This PR introduces two complementary features: 1) concise runbook linking — a compact, single-line runbook summary + link that surfaces the most likely next steps and ownership; 2) autodiagnostics context enrichment — the bot now attaches a short SLO/metric snapshot + top 3 likely root-cause signals (previously computed by the slo-toolkit) to the notification so responders get immediate context for common classes of failures. Changes are backwards-compatible and opt-in via a new org-level incident-bot config flag (runbook_mode: compact|full). High-level changes: - New runbook summarizer that extracts the runbook title, short description (<=140 chars), and primary pager/ownership tag. - Minor templating changes to the incident message payload to support compact mode. - Integration with slo-toolkit endpoint to fetch SLO snapshot and top signals; fallback to legacy context when endpoint times out. - Added unit and integration tests for templating and the new config. - Updated docs and runbook examples with recommended compact templates. Rollout plan: - Feature gated behind incident-bot config flag; default remains "full" for orgs not opting in. - Canary: enable compact mode for staging and two smaller teams for 48h; monitor oncall feedback and message action usage. - Full rollout: gradual enable across orgs after no regressions. Testing and verification: - Added unit tests to validate summary length boundaries and markdown escaping. - End-to-end tests added using the incident-bot test harness to simulate SLO snapshot failures and ensure graceful fallback. - Manual verification on staging: message formatting, link resolution, and Slack threading behavior. Checklist: - [x] Implementation complete - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Docs updated - [x] Canaried in staging - [x] Reviewed and approved by SRE and DX Impact: Improves on-call triage speed by surfacing a compact runbook and immediate SLO signals; reduces initial message noise. Related: ENG-8423 (compact runbook UX), SRE-1291 (SLO snapshot standardization), SUP-6142 (support ticket requesting shorter runbook links).

feat(slo-toolkit): add SLO snapshot fetch + top-signal extraction adapter

test: add unit + integration tests for messaging and fallback
docs: update incident-bot runbook docs and quickstart
review_comments: Ethan Cole: Nice direction. Can we ensure the summarizer never truncates a critical ownership tag? Suggest adding an explicit ownership extractor.
Priya Natarajan: Added ownership extractor and prioritized ownership tokens in the summarizer. Also added tests to assert presence of owner tags.
Marta Ruiz: Please make sure the slo-toolkit call is non-blocking for the main notify path; I prefer a 200ms timeout and fallback to legacy context.
Priya Natarajan: Implemented 200ms timeout with async fetch and graceful fallback. Integration tests simulate timeouts.
Jordan Lee: Docs look good. One nit: example compact template should show how to include incident severity. Fixed in last commit.
Ethan Cole: Approved after small nits addressed. Verified staging canary messages — compact mode looks clean and SLO snapshot shows correctly.
release_notes: Incident-bot: adds opt-in 'compact' runbook mode that posts a one-line runbook summary + link and enriches notifications with a short SLO snapshot and top-3 signals. Configured via incident-bot.runbook_mode; defaults to 'full'. Backwards-compatible.
notes_for_oncall: When enabled, compact runbook messages will include a short summary and a link labeled 'Runbook'. If SLO snapshot fetch fails, incident-bot falls back to legacy verbose context. Use the 'More details' action on the message to fetch the full runbook and diagnostics.
